instructions:
Each item is an ontology term that a column of sample metadata in a gene
expression study can mean. Write up to 5 aliases for each term: other ways a
researcher would write that same variable as a column header in sample
metadata.

Good aliases:
- common abbreviations and acronyms ("sbp" for systolic blood pressure)
- shorter everyday phrasings ("systolic bp", "visual acuity")
- the plain name of the quantity when the term's label is wordy
  ("intraocular pressure" for "intraocular pressure measurement")

Rules:
- An alias must mean the same variable as the term: not a broader or narrower
  one, and not a related one.
- No values ("male", "high"), units on their own, gene or tool names, or
  dataset-specific codes.
- No alias that only rewords the label trivially (plural, case,
  punctuation). Those are matched already.
- Fewer is better than wrong. If a term has no natural alias, return an empty
  list.

Examples:
- systolic blood pressure -> ["sbp", "systolic bp", "systolic pressure"]
- intraocular pressure measurement -> ["intraocular pressure", "iop"]
- visual acuity measurement -> ["visual acuity", "va"]

items.label: paraffin specimen
items.definition: a specimen that is output of a paraffin storage process in which specimen is embedded in paraffin

items.label: fresh specimen
items.definition: a specimen that is output of a specimen creation process used for an investigation without storage.

items.label: agar stab specimen
items.definition: a specimen that is output of a process that cell culture inoculated into agar for long term storage.

items.label: spike-in quality control role
items.definition: a reference substance role that is borne by a material entity with a known amount which is mixed into the evaluant of assays for quality control or data normalization purposes

items.label: dye swap quality control role
items.definition: a reference substance role that is borne by a material entity used in a dye swap design experiment for quality control or data normalization purposes

items.label: validation by reverse transcription PCR design
items.definition: a study design in which checks the accuracy or the quality of the result of an assay  by comparing with reverse transcription PCR results

items.label: validation by real time PCR design
items.definition: a study design in which the accuracy or the quality of the result of an assay is checked by comparing with real time PCR results

items.label: q-value
items.definition:
A quantitative confidence value that measures the minimum false discovery rate that is incurred when calling that test significant. 
To compute q-values, it is necessary to know the p-value produced by a test and possibly set a false discovery rate level.

items.label: cell specimen
items.definition: A specimen primarily composed of cells collected from a multicellular organism or a cell culture

items.label: specimen with known storage state
items.definition: A specimen for which it is known whether it has been subjected to storage of a specified type.

items.label: latitude coordinate measurement datum
items.definition: A measurement datum that is the measure of the latitude coordinate of a site.

items.label: longitude coordinate measurement datum
items.definition: A measurement datum that is the measure of the longitude coordinate of a site.

items.label: in-situ hybridization assay
items.definition: An assay that localizes a specific DNA or RNA sequence within a portion or section of tissue using artificially induced nucleic hybridization.

items.label: immunoprecipitation assay
items.definition: An analyte assay in which an input material is mixed with antibodies and bound antigen:antibody complexes are separated out using immunoprecipitation. items.label: immunocytochemistry
items.definition: An immuno staining assay in which samples of intact cells are examined that have had most, if not all, of their surrounding extracellular matrix removed

items.label: tissue section thickness
items.definition: A length measurement datum that is the result of an assay measuring the thickness of a tissue section.

items.label: differential expression analysis data
items.definition: The results of a differential expression analysis.

items.label: cyclic immunofluoroescence assay
items.definition: A type of microscopy assay resulting in highly multiplexed immunofluorescence imaging through sequential rounds of imaging followed by fluorophore inactivation.

items.label: autofluorescence assay
items.definition: A fluorescence detection assay in which the light that is naturally emitted by a sample is visualized after excitation of the sample with light at a suitable wavelength.

items.label: co-detection by indexing assay
items.definition: A multiplexed fluorescent antibody imaging assay that involves a highly multiplexed analysis of up to 40 proteins in a tissue using cyclic detection of DNA-indexed antibody panels.

items.label: liquid chromatography mass spectrometry assay
items.definition: A mass spectrometry assay where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before being converted into ions which are characterized by using mass spectrometry based on their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

items.label: lightsheet fluorescence microscopy assay
items.definition: A fluorescence microscopy that involves capturing of photons emitted by fluorophores excited with a thin sheet of laser light in a sample only in a relatively narrow plane by a detection objective oriented perpendicularly to the light sheet and imaged onto a detection device such as a CCD camera.

items.label: matrix assisted laser desorption ionization imaging mass spectrometry assay
items.definition: A mass spectrometry assay that involves collection of spatially resolved mass spectra of a sample during microscopy where a pulse laser is used to produce both ionisation and vaporization. items.label: multiplexed ion beam imaging assay
items.definition: A cytometry time of flight assay in which molecules of interest on or in cells are imaged through a system in which samples are labeled with multiple different rare-earth tagged antibodies. items.label: single-cell combinatorial indexing RNA sequencing assay
items.definition: A single-cell transcription profiling by RNA sequencing assay that involves single cell combinatorial indexing ('sci-') strategy to profile the transcriptomes of single cells or nuclei without single cell isolation.

items.label: Olink assay
items.definition: A proximity extension assay that uses quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) technology to determine the concentration/presence of proteins using a high-multiplex, high-throughput protein biomarker platform. The assay utilizes two distinct oligonucleotide-labeled antibodies (‘probes’) that bi

items.label: assay kit
items.definition: A device that consists of reagents and devices that enable the performance of a specific type of assay, which could, in addition, require specific instruments not included in the kit.

items.label: specimen
items.definition: A material entity that is collected for potential use as an input upon which measurements or observations are performed.

items.label: data transformation
items.definition: A data transformation is a process which produces output data from input data - e.g. the application of a clustering protocol to microarray data or the application of a statistical testing method on a primary data set to determine a p-value.

items.label: biexponential transformation
items.definition: A biexponential transformation is a data transformation that, for each (one dimensional) real number input x, outputs an approximation (found, e.g. with the Newton's method) to a solution y of the equation B(y)-x=0, where B denotes a b transformation.

items.label: loess transformation
items.definition: A loess transformation is a data transformation that takes as input a collection of real number pairs (x, y) and, after performing (one or more) loess fittings, utilizes the resulting curves to transform each (x, y) in the input into (x, y-f(x)) where f(x) is one of the fitted curves.

items.label: normalization data transformation
items.definition: A normalization data transformation is a data transformation that has objective normalization.

items.label: nucleic acid hybridization
items.definition: a planned process by which totally or partially complementary, single-stranded nucleic acids are  combined into a single molecule called heteroduplex or homoduplex to an extent depending on the amount of complementarity.

items.label: DNA sequencer
items.definition: A DNA sequencer is an instrument that determines the order of deoxynucleotides in deoxyribonucleic acid sequences.

items.label: array scanner
items.definition: An processed material which acquires images of fluorescence (induced with lasers) from labeled molecules on the surface of the microarray chip

items.label: arrayer
items.definition: a device which deposits biological material onto a substrate in a defined pattern.

items.label: centrifuge
items.definition: A device with a rapidly rotating container that applies centrifugal force to its contents

items.label: computer
items.definition: A computer is an instrument which manipulates (stores, retrieves, and processes) data according to a list of instructions.

items.label: heating block
items.definition: A heating block is an instrument or part of an instrument which raises or maintains the temperature of a sample to a defined constant temperature during certain parts of an assay

items.label: homogenizer
items.definition: A homogenizer is an instrument for the homogenization of various types of material, such as tissue, plant, food, soil, and many others.

items.label: hybridization chamber
items.definition: A device which is used to maintain constant contact of a liquid on an array.  This can be either a glass vial or slide.

items.label: hybridization station
items.definition: An instrument which is used to maintain the temperature of one or more hybridization_chamber(s) at a defined, constant temperature.

items.label: liquid handler
items.definition: A device that is used for automated liquid transfer and handling.

items.label: oligonucleotide synthesizer
items.definition: An instrument used to chemically synthesize oligonucleotides.

items.label: sonicator
items.definition: An instrument that converts a variable electrical current to mechanical vibration of a metallic probe. The instrument is used for the lysis of cells, the mixing of compounds or solutions, or to create emulsions.

items.label: spectrophotometer
items.definition: A spectrophotometer is an instrument that measures the intensity of light as a function of the color, or more specifically, the wavelength of light, transmitted by a substance.

items.label: thermal cycler
items.definition: An instrument that is capable of repeatedly altering and maintaining specific temperatures for defined periods of time.

items.label: vacuum dryer
items.definition: An instrument which removes liquid by the application of negative pressure,  i.e. vacuum.

items.label: vortexer
items.definition: A vortexer is an instrument that mixes small vials of liquid by creating a rotation of the liquid around its own center. items.label: water bath
items.definition: A water bath is a temperature control bath in which a water acts as contact medium enabling temperature transfer from the heating element or cooling element to the sample. The temperature can be controlled in the 0 to 100 degree centigrade range (under normal pressure).

items.label: tumor grading
items.definition: An assay that determines the grade (severity/stage) of a tumor sample, used in cancer biology to describe abnormalities/qualities of tumor cells or tissues. Values can be described by terms from NCI Thesaurus.

items.label: collecting specimen from organism
items.definition: a process with the objective to obtain a material entity that was part of an organism for potential future use in an investigation

items.label: group assignment
items.definition: group assignment is a process which has an organism as specified input and during which a role is assigned

items.label: histological assay
items.definition: An assay that uses visual examination of cells or tissue (or images of them) to make an assessment regarding a quality of the cells or tissue. This assay can include steps of staining, imaging, and judgement.

items.label: lavage
items.definition: A protocol application to separate cells and/or cellular secretions from an anatomical space by the introduction and removal of fluid

items.label: cell culture supernatant
items.definition: Supernatant of a cell culture is a material entity which contains media, supplements, and secreted products of the cells and becomes the environment of cultivated cell.

items.label: infection process
items.definition: the detrimental process in which an infectious agent colonizes or replicates in a host environment

items.label: pathologic process
items.definition: abnormal, harmful processes caused by or associated with a disease

items.label: concentration of
items.definition: A quality inhering in a substance by virtue of the amount of the bearer's there is mixed with another substance.

items.label: biological sex
items.definition: An organismal quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ability to undergo sexual reproduction in order to differentiate the individuals or types involved. [ MGED:MGED ]

items.label: morphology
items.definition: A property of a single physical entity describing the entity's size or shape or structure.

items.label: deviation(from_normal)
items.definition: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the whether the bearer differs from normal or average.

items.label: amount
items.definition: The number of entities of this type that are part of the whole organism.

items.label: mass
items.definition: A physical quality of the amount of matter in a material.

items.label: rate
items.definition: A quality of a single process inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's occurrence per unit time.

items.label: viability
items.definition: An organismal quality inhering in a bearer or a population by virtue of the bearer's disposition to survive and develop normally or the number of surviving individuals in a given population.

items.label: female
items.definition: A biological sex quality inhering in an individual or a population that only produces gametes that can be fertilised by male gametes.

items.label: male
items.definition: A biological sex quality inhering in an individual or a population whose sex organs contain only male gametes.

items.label: abnormal
items.definition: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's deviation from normal or average.

items.label: normal
items.definition: The state of the organism when it functions optimally without evidence of disease.

items.label: increased amount
items.definition: An amount which is relatively high.
synonyms: present in greater numbers in organism

items.label: increased rate
items.definition: A rate which is relatively high.

items.label: concentrated
items.definition: A concentration quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's exhibiting concentration.

items.label: increased concentration
items.definition: A concentration which is higher relative to the normal or average.

items.label: decreased concentration
items.definition: A concentration which is lower relative to the normal or average.

items.label: process quality
items.definition: A quality which inheres in an process.

items.label: hermaphrodite
items.definition: An organism having both male and female sexual characteristics and organs.

items.label: ploidy
items.definition: A cellular quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's number of homologous sets of chromosomes in the nucleus or primary chromosome-containing compartment of the cell, each set essentially coding for all the biological traits of the organism. [ Wikipedia:http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ploi

items.label: polyploid
items.definition: A ploidy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's containing more than two homologous sets of chromosomes.

items.label: triploid
items.definition: A polyploidy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's containing three homologous sets of chromosomes.

items.label: tetraploid
items.definition: A polyploidy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's containing four homologous sets of chromosomes.

items.label: hexaploid
items.definition: A polyploidy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's containing four homologous sets of chromosomes.

items.label: euploid
items.definition: A ploidy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's containing an integral multiple of the monoploid number, possibly excluding the sex-determining chromosomes.

items.label: dead
items.definition: Irreversible cessation of all bodily functions, manifested by absence of spontaneous breathing and total loss of cardiovascular and cerebral functions.

items.label: having extra processual parts
items.definition: A quality of a process inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having additional processual parts.

items.label: extra or missing processual parts
items.definition: A quality of a process inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's processual parts.

items.label: pathological
items.definition: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being abnormal and having a destructive effect on living tissue.

items.label: phenotypic sex
items.definition: An organismal quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's physical expression of sexual characteristics.

items.label: molecular quality
items.definition: A quality which inheres in a molecular entity, a single molecule, atom, ion, radical etc.

items.label: life cycle
items.definition: An entire span of an organism's life. In metazoans, commences with the zygote stage and ends with the death of the organism.
